newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE-N.Y. teacher gives aerobics his own flair.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-N.Y. teacher gives aerobics his own flair.

text.p: For some, going to the gym is a drag. For aerobics instructor Anthony Truly, it's a drag show.

Truly can be found teaching aerobics classes, decked out in a tousled platinum blond wig and tight red leggings, with tassles dangling from his chest and his platform sneakers. Sometimes, for fun, he stuffs a sports bra with falsies.

As his 40-odd students pant and perspire through a grueling hour of push-ups and tummy crunches, Truly sashays around the room, batting his long, gold eyelashes, striking poses and delivering catty comments.
"Did you all hear Michael Jackson is going to be a mother?" he asks as his students at Crunch, one of New York's hippest gyms, pause to chuckle through their pain.

Truly, a former ballet dancer and Ice Capades choreographer from Memphis, Tennessee, is a dominatrix of exercise, correcting his students' posture and pushing them to work harder in his two trademark classes -- "Abs, Thighs and Gossip" and "Aerobics with Attitude."
GIGGLING AND COY, LIKE THE GIRL NEXT DOOR

But he is also the girl next door, giggling and coy. While many men take his classes, Truly contends he is striving for a "sister thing" where "girls can come and dish about their boyfriends and tell jokes."
"He's the sweetest person," said Madalyn Castle, who has been taking Truly's classes since he began teaching at Crunch in 1992. "His choreography is so ... cute!"

At the end of a body-sculpting class, Truly leads an exercise on "how to take a compliment." Sitting cross-legged, he urges women in the class to toss their hair and cover their mouths as they giggle.

A short, athletically fit man with a goatee, Truly compares his professional persona to RuPaul, a flamboyant transvestite, and Dennis Rodman, an equally flamboyant professional basketball player. Like them, he takes his role as diva very, very seriously. He owns 25 wigs and packs a gym bag full of campy accoutrements such as false fangs, finger cymbals, chiffon scarves and strobe lights.
He strives to help his students live out their fantasies while they work off their flab. "Rock'n'roll is dead, drugs and sex are out," he said. "So I give people an outlet."

The dance routines in "Aerobics with Attitude" are hyper-sexual, Las Vegas-meets-Madonna. He teaches a new combination every couple of weeks and has a name for each of the 22 routines in his repertoire. There is his Cyber-Funk of robot-like moves set to hi-tech club music, the Susan Lucci-Funk inspired by Truly's favourite soap opera star and the Home Perm-Funk, a must for anyone who has ever given herself a bad hairdo.
LEAVES YOU FEELING SEXUAL AND SELF-CONFIDENT
"I leave the class feeling sexual and self-confident," said Jennifer Baumgardner, who loathed aerobics before she met Truly. "It's as if you've been flirted with for an hour."

Not everyone is turned on by the idea of a fitness queen. Before the Crunch chain opened its five New York locations four years ago, Truly's idea for campy classes was rejected by a number of the city's gyms.

"You wouldn't believe the animosity I still get," Truly said as beefy weightlifters gawked at him from the other side of a glass wall in the Crunch studio. But Truly thinks his time has come. A regular contributor to Crunch's show on the ESPN cable channel, he said he is talking to other networks about hosting his own fitness programme.
"It doesn't matter how beautiful or skinny you are. Everyone has their insecurities," he said. "It's my goal to take those away, to make you feel fabulous."
His students do, indeed, leave the gym feeling like a million bucks. "This is pure physical joy," actor Fabian Blue said. "If only life could be like this 24 hours a day."
